comparison: Strong agreement on azide methodology findings (C66-C94). Both identify the critical difference between +azide and -azide conditions as explaining the Gainey et al. discrepancy. OpenEval emphasizes statistical support and time-course analysis; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the head-to-head comparison and note azide is essential for transgenerational inheritance.

OpenEval R2 addresses methodological discrepancy explanation (C65, C69, C75-C76, C88-C89) which overlaps with peer R1's broader discussion of protocol differences. Both support the finding that protocol variations explain the Gainey et al. results, though peer review groups this with the azide findings more comprehensively.

Strong agreement on P11 expression and its role in transgenerational inheritance (C13-C15, C107-C130). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative expression data and condition-dependent P11 levels; peer reviewers explicitly affirm temperature-dependent P11 expression and note this provides additional explanation for discrepancies. Both highlight that P11 expression is sensitive to culture conditions.

OpenEval R6 focuses on E. coli-P11 sufficiency experiments (C113-C120); peer R2 encompasses broader P11 findings including these experiments. Both support P11's sufficiency for transgenerational avoidance, though peer review integrates this with temperature-dependent expression findings.

Partial overlap on experimental replication (C103-C106 in OpenEval R4; C104-C105, C60-C61, C206-C207 in peer R6). OpenEval emphasizes consistent P0 and F2 avoidance under specific conditions; peer reviewers affirm detailed, rigorous, and reproducible protocols across all experiments.

Strong agreement on genetic dissection of sRNA pathway (C131-C140). OpenEval details meg-1;meg-3, nrde-3, and rde-3/mut-2 mutant experiments showing pathway separation; peer reviewers affirm the genetic requirements identified and note solid results, though without detailed critique of specific mutants.

Strong agreement on comprehensive genetic analysis (C141-C147, C195-C201). OpenEval enumerates ~40 mutants across six studies establishing complex multi-component mechanism; peer reviewers consistently affirm the extensive mutant analyses defining both PA14 and C. elegans factors, describing results as compelling and powerful.

OpenEval R9 addresses tissue-specific rescue experiments (C202-C203) which are included in peer R4's broader affirmation of genetic analysis. OpenEval notes lack of detailed experimental evidence in manuscript excerpt; peer reviewers endorse overall genetic findings without specific comment on tissue localization.

Strong agreement on conservation across species (C173-C179, C191-C194). OpenEval emphasizes sequence-matching requirements and convergence on maco-1; peer reviewers explicitly affirm results with additional Pseudomonas species and new sRNAs, strengthening physiological relevance arguments.

OpenEval R11 focuses on maco-1 mechanistic role (C180-C190); peer R5 encompasses broader conservation findings including downstream targets. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic evidence through expression, mutants, and epistasis; peer reviewers affirm overall conservation results without specific maco-1 discussion.

Strong agreement on P11's bacterial function and ecological rationale (C157-C170, C208). OpenEval connects nitrogen fixation, biofilm formation, and ammonia production to worm behavior; peer reviewer explicitly engages with biological explanation, finding it plausible and consistent with bacterial physiology, suggesting further testable predictions.

Agreement on conservation and broad significance (C17-C19, C216-C217). OpenEval infers ecological importance from conservation; peer reviewers explicitly affirm broad interest across genetics, epigenetics, and learned behavior, endorsing physiological importance and relevance beyond the specific system.

OpenEval R13 includes biomarker hypothesis (C209-C211); peer R7 discusses biological rationale. Both address ecological significance, though OpenEval presents biomarker function as inference while peer reviewer focuses on plausibility of environmental regulation.

Strong agreement on reproducibility (C60-C61, C206-C207). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across studies and inclusion of wild-type controls; peer reviewers explicitly affirm detailed, rigorous, and reproducible protocols, describing the work as excellent and well-written.

OpenEval R3 addresses azide effect generalization to PF15 (C90-C92); peer R5 discusses broader conservation across Pseudomonas species. Both support generalization beyond PA14, strengthening the conclusion that findings are not strain-specific.

OpenEval R15 addresses pathway independence and interpretation of experimental results (C153-C156, C171-C172). No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly discussing this methodological point, though it is implicit in peer acceptance of the genetic dissection experiments.

OpenEval R16 synthesizes different pathways and timescales from prior literature (C40-C44, C100-C102, C151-C152). No corresponding peer review evaluation found explicitly discussing this literature synthesis, though peer reviewers affirm the study provides additional understanding of differences between naïve preference, learned preference, and transgenerational inheritance.
